newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-CHEN COMPETES DESPITE INJURY.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-CHEN COMPETES DESPITE INJURY.

text.p: China's former title winner Chen Lu said on Tuesday she was already focusing on next year's Olympic Games in Japan and had little chance of a high finish at the world figure skating championships this week.
The 1995 champion has returned to competition with only a month of preparation after a four-month break because of a foot injury.
She became her country's first champion in this sport two years ago, then surrendered her crown in an exciting battle against American Michelle Kwan in Canada last year.

This season a stress fracture of her right instep seriously curtailed her build-up. She finished only 11th in her qualifying group on Monday, completing just one triple jump, falling once and scaling down four other intended triples to singles.
"I am not fully prepared for these championships but I will not withdraw because it is vital for qualifying for next year's Olympic Games," she said.
"I hope for a top-24 placing here to be sure of qualifying for the Olympics but I will try my best for a higher position though I am not thinking about a final place.
The main event does not begin until Friday. "It is important that I train well during these two or three days," she said.

"After these championships we will start training for the Olympics, to see if I can get the first gold medal in history for China at the Winter Games. That is the goal for myself, my coach and the federation."
Chen suffered the injury at the Skate Canada competition early in October. "I felt a small pain, then landing a jump it felt very painful," she said.
It turned out to be a recurrence of the injury that forced her out of the 1994 world championships in Japan. She returned home for treatment and only resumed skating last month.
Chen also confirmed reports that she had problems with her national federation over money she earned from skating away from home, and that she had fallen out with coach Zhu Li-ming.
"There were regulations in China about money that I did not know about and my coach and I also had a conflict," she said.
"But now everything has been sorted out and the federation, my coach and myself are very comfortable."
